messages:
Liam: Quick heads-up — after the kernel swap last night (fused_attn_fast) we're seeing p99 tail spikes on longer sequences when GPU util crosses ~78%. Pasted a microprof sample below, but tl;dr: throughput up, tail latency worse.

Maya: Can you drop the numbers? p95/p99 and util distribution pls.

Liam: Sure — grab from the 2h window around the rollout:
```
window: 02:10-04:10
requests: 24k
seq_len median: 512
kv_cache_hit: 0.86
gpu_util mean: 72%
gpu_util 90/95/99: 68/76/82
latency p50/p95/p99 (ms): 48 / 210 / 820
microbatch size: dynamic (1-8, median 3)
kernel active: fused_attn_fast (fallbacks to matmul_v2 at long seq)
```
Observation: p95 ok, but p99 jumps near those util hotspots. microprof shows long kernel stalls when KV miss + big seq.

Jordan: Hmm — fused_attn_fast is optimized for small-medium seqs, high throughput. It does aggressive per-thread tiling; when KV cache is cold or we have KV miss churn it serializes some IO and stalls. So util high -> queuing -> more long tails.

Sophia: Two levers: (A) lower target_util / reserve a slab for tails; (B) probe-based admission: allow util to float up fast but probe-only accept N requests and fall back when p99 passes threshold. Pros/cons?

Liam: Right. Quick simulation I ran:
```
config A: target_util=0.65, reserve=0.15 -> p99 ~420ms, throughput -12%
config B: probe_guard: probe_rate=0.05, probe_window=30s, p99_thresh=600ms -> p99 ~560ms, throughput -5% but occasional 700-900ms spikes during probe failures
```

Andre: If customer SLA is p99<500ms we probably need config A. But that hits unit cost. Could do hybrid: reserve slab for critical traffic (enterprise tenants) + probe for best-effort.

Maya: What about microbatch sizing? If median microbatch=3, maybe increase min_batch to 4 to reduce kernel switch frequency. Any regression risk?

Jordan: Increasing min_batch helps throughput and reduces dispatch churn which reduces kernel selection thrash. But it increases queuing latency for single-stream short requests (p50). We can do request-type-aware batching: small prompt routes to small-kernel fast path, long sequences to reserved slab.

Liam: Also KV cache behavior: when cache hit drops below ~0.8 we see far more memory copies. Suggest we add a KV-prefetch heuristic: if seq_len>1024 and kv_hit<0.9, prefetch next chunk and force matmul_v2 path proactively.

Sophia: Can we implement a soft fallback: if a request triggers >2 kernel fallbacks within X seconds, tag the model session and route future tokens to conservative kernel for Y minutes. That avoids repeated tail penalties.

Jordan: Implementation sketch:
```
// per-session state
session.fallback_count += 1
if session.fallback_count > 2:
  session.kernel_hint = "stable_matmul_v2"
  session.hint_expires = now + 10m
```
Edge: need to garbage collect sessions for stateless workloads.
```

Maya: Ops questions: how to test without full rollout? Canary with traffic shaping: send 10% production but bump long-seq fraction to amplify tail signals.

Liam: I queued an A/B canary for tomorrow 06:00 UTC. Plan:
- 10% traffic, but 4x long-seq weight
- measure p50/p95/p99 and gpu_util spread
- enable session kernel hint in canary only

sre-bot: [alert] p99 > 750ms observed during previous canary at 2026-03-12T06:14:02Z — auto-rollback happened.

Andre: For rollout policy, add automatic fallback to matmul_v2 when p99 > threshold and util>80% for 3 consecutive windows.

Sophia: We should tune SLO enforcement window: use 60s windows for p99 triggers (fast reaction) but require 3 windows to avoid noisy rollback.

Liam: Action items:
- Jordan: add session kernel hint + GC (PR)
- Maya: schedule canary with long-seq weighting, collect microprof traces
- Sophia: draft admission config param set (target_util, reserve_pct, probe_rate, p99_thresh, reaction_windows)
- Andre: build fallback rollback rule in rollout agent

Liam: tagging @Jordan @Maya @Sophia @Andre — let's sync 30m after canary results. :eyes:
